subject: procD.pgls null model and interpretation of r2

messages.author: 674ab04cee310e45
messages.subject: procD.pgls null model and interpretation of r2
parts:
Hi all,

I've hit a few snags in my analysis and I'm hoping someone can shed some light on a couple of geomorph-related questions. The first is pretty straightforward: is there a way to run a null model through the procD.pgls function in geomorph? I'm trying to separately phylogenetically correct a multivariate (shape) and a univariate (size) data set. While the gls function in 'nlme' will run on a null model, it cannot accommodate multivariate data sets. I feel uncomfortable comparing data phylogenetically corrected in two separate packages as I'm not sure the implementation is equivalent. 

Secondly, it has come to my attention that the interpretation of the r2 value is not equivalent between OLS and GLS -- does geomorph incorporate a correction for this or is the reported r2 value computed as it would be with an OLS? Essentially, is it valid to interpret the coefficient of determination from procD.pgls as a percentage of the total variance of the dependent variable explained by the regression?  

Any help is much appreciated!

Thanks,
Sarah

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] procD.pgls null model and interpretation of r2
parts: I've hit a few snags in my analysis and I'm hoping someone can shed some light on a couple of geomorph-related questions. The first is pretty straightforward: is there a way to run a null model through the procD.pgls function in geomorph?

There really is no way to "run a null model”, as procD.pgls needs at least two models - one a null and another with some independent variable - to compare.  Are you asking for linear model coefficients?  If so, then procD.pgls gives you the tools to do that.

For example, follow the example in procD.pgls up until the part you have created pleth.pgls.

Then, pleth.pgls$Pcor is the matrix for phylogenetic correction; pleth.pgls$Y is the matrix of shape data; pleth.pgls$X is the design matrix.  You can do something like this:

P <- pleth.plgs$Pcor
X.null <- as.matrix(pleth.pgls$X[,1] # just the intercept
Y <- pleth.pgls$Y

lm.fit(P%*%X.null, P%*%Y)

which will give you coefficients, fitted values, etc.

Secondly, it has come to my attention that the interpretation of the r2 value is not equivalent between OLS and GLS -- does geomorph incorporate a correction for this or is the reported r2 value computed as it would be with an OLS? Essentially, is it valid to interpret the coefficient of determination from procD.pgls as a percentage of the total variance of the dependent variable explained by the regression?

procD.pgls calculates R-squared values as SSeffect/SStotal, where SS is based on phylogenetically corrected values.  So, no, the values will not be the same as in OLS.  To my way of thinking, it is valid, but I would change your last part of the question to "percentage of the total varianceation of the dependent variable explained by the regression, after adjusting values due to phylogenetic relatedness.”

Hope that helps
Mike
